div.head: Duns 7
div.ab: Hors man sceal gyldan mid XXX scill.' oððe be ðam ladian; myran mid XX scill.' oððe be ðam, ⁊ wintersteal ealswa; wilde weorf mid XII scill.' oððe be ðam; oxan mid XXX p.', cu mid XXIIII p.', swyn mid VIII p.', man mid punde, sceap mid scill.', gat mid II p.'

Equus debet reddi triginta sol., uel secundum id negari; equa uiginti sol., uel per id negari; et ƿintersteal et ƿildeƿeorf XII sol., uel ita negari; bos XXX den.; uacca XXIIII den.; porcus VIII den.; homo XX sol.; ouis un. sol.

(Vom Werthe eines jeden Stück Vieh, wenn sie verloren gehen. lq) Ein männliches Pferd soll man [wenn deshalb verklagt] mit 30 [Mercischen] Schillingen bezahlen oder demgemäss Reinigungsbeweis erbringen; eine Stute mit 20 Schillingen oder demgemäss [sich reinigen]; und ebenso einen einjährigen Hengst[?]; eine [noch] ungezähmte Stute[?] mit 12 Schill. oder demgemäss [sich reinigen]; einen Ochsen mit 30 Pfennig, eine Kuh mit 24 Pfennig, ein Schwein mit 8 Pfennig, einen Sklaven mit 1 Pfund, ein Schaf mit 1 Schilling, eine Ziege mit 2 Pfennig.

(Of the value of each head of livestock, if they are lost. lq) A male horse shall be paid for [if one is accused over it] with 30 [Mercian] shillings, or a clearing proof made accordingly; a mare with 20 shillings, or [clear oneself] accordingly; and likewise a yearling stallion[?]; an untamed [as yet] mare[?] with 12 shillings, or [clear oneself] accordingly; an ox with 30 pence, a cow with 24 pence, a pig with 8 pence, a slave with 1 pound, a sheep with 1 shilling, a goat with 2 pence.

A [male] horse [in the event of compensation in a legal suit] is paid for with thirty shillings or [relief gained] by [successful] exculpation; a mare with twenty shillings, or [the charge] exculpated; and also a one year stallion [?]; an untamed [?] mare with twelve shillings, or exculpated; an ox with thirty shillings, a cow with twenty-four pennies, a pig with eight pennies; a man [slave] with a pound, sheep with a shilling, a goat with two pennies.

U: translator unrecorded: check; Word order from Ld: B reads ‘sceap oðre … gyldan [i.e. 7.1] mid s., gat m. II p'’, which Liebermann calls senseless, probably a line skipped in the exemplar and inserted from its margin in the wrong place (the Quadripartitus shows the exemplar already had this error). B adds ‘l'’ (i.e. ‘oððe’) after ‘be ðam’, which Liebermann strikes following Ld and the Quadripartitus. The Quadripartitus's ‘homo XX sol.’ is Norman, Liebermann notes. Liebermann compares VI As 6.1–2 and 8.5.

‘Hengst’ Schmid. Dass das Wort hier, wie Mittelenglisch und equus Hn 76, 7f, diese engere Bed. hat, folgt nur aus Ggs. zum folgenden
‘Stallion’ Schmid. That the word here, as in Middle English and equus Hn 76, 7f, has this narrower meaning follows only from the contrast with what follows

Dass der kleine 4 Pf.-Schilling hier gemeint ist, folgt aus der Bewertung des Pferdes (s. d. Gl 15) zu 120 Pf. anderswo, aus den Preisen für Kuh und Schwein, die nur dann runde Schillingsummen ergeben, und daraus, dass nur so der Preis des Sklaven bzw. Schweins bei Westsachsen und Dunsæten 60 bzw. 2 Schilling beträgt; endlich grenzten die Dunsæte an Mercien, nicht an Wessex; s. Einl. 8

That the small shilling of 4 pence is meant here follows from the valuation of the horse (see that word in Gl 15) at 120 pence elsewhere, from the prices for cow and pig, which yield round sums in shillings only on this reckoning, and from the fact that only thus does the price of the slave and of the pig respectively amount to 60 and 2 shillings among both West Saxons and Dunsæte; finally, the Dunsæte bordered on Mercia, not on Wessex; see Introduction 8

Zu Archiv 288 ergänze: winter- für ‘einjährig’ s. winterling ‘Rind von 1 Jahr’, yearling ‘einjährig Tier’, twinter, thrinter ‘2 (3)jährig Schaf’. Ein Gutsinventar vom Ende 10. Jhs. (oder vielleicht etwas später) verzeichnet IX winterstellas ⁊ I fedelsswin (Mastschwein; Birch n. 1128), leider ohne Schlüssel, was es meint. Ein Bauer bei Southampton um 1130 heisst Willelmus Wynterstial; Haskins in Mél. Bémont 81

So Lye, Thorpe, Toller; ‘an animal’ Sweet; Q did not understand the word. To Archiv 288 add: for winter- meaning ‘one year old’ see winterling ‘bullock of 1 year’, yearling ‘one-year-old animal’, twinter, thrinter ‘2 (3)-year-old sheep’. An estate inventory of the end of the 10th cent. (or perhaps somewhat later) lists IX winterstellas ⁊ I fedelsswin (fattening pig; Birch n. 1128), unfortunately without any key to what it means. A peasant near Southampton c. 1130 is called Willelmus Wynterstial; Haskins in Mél. Bémont 81
